findings.evidence: document_service.py:333-340 returns None when the name query has no rows; api_app.py:618-621 immediately uses the result for membership and append, and web/src/hooks/document-hooks.ts:419-423 sends only doc_ids.
findings.reason: ID-only deletion reaches a membership test on None and returns a server error before processing the supplied IDs.

findings.evidence: The bulk query filters only non-unique Document.name, while api_app.py:609-618 has the token tenant but does not pass it and api_app.py:636-660 deletes every returned document using that document's owning tenant.
findings.reason: Same cross-tenant deletion defect as f12; the security pass supplied the strongest authorization trace.

findings.evidence: The lazy ordered query at line 32 is indexed once for every obsolete version at line 36 before the batch delete.
findings.reason: Same remaining linear-read defect as f5; the simplicity candidate stated the query behavior more precisely.

findings.evidence: The plural service helper returns None for no rows although its changed caller unconditionally treats the value as a mutable collection.
findings.reason: Same ID-only deletion regression as f1; merged into the more directly caller-anchored finding.

findings.evidence: Indexing user_canvas_version[i] repeatedly applies a per-index lazy-query fetch, leaving one database read per obsolete version before delete_by_ids.
findings.request: Select all obsolete version IDs in one query before the bulk delete.
findings.reason: Validation reduced P2 to P3 because writes are now batched and the remaining defect is a performance shortfall rather than incorrect deletion; it was still posted as a nit.

findings.evidence: No-match name lookup returns None and api_app.py:619-621 performs membership and append on it.
findings.reason: Duplicate of f1, which carries the concrete existing ID-only caller evidence.

findings.evidence: The name-only predicate returns every globally matching non-unique document name and the route does not constrain the result to the API-token tenant.
findings.reason: Duplicate of f12's cross-tenant destructive authorization defect.

findings.evidence: The existing frontend sends {doc_ids: [...]} without doc_names, making the helper's None result flow into a failing membership test.
findings.reason: Duplicate of f1; its frontend evidence was retained in the posted blocker.

findings.evidence: Unlike the old single-row helper, the new IN query expands one requested name to all matching rows, and the route deletes all of them without checking the token tenant.
findings.reason: Duplicate of f12; merged under the security pass's authorization-focused anchor.

findings.evidence: The new batching collects IDs through repeated indexed accesses to the lazy query, retaining O(n) reads despite the stated goal.
findings.reason: Duplicate of f5 and merged into its more implementation-specific explanation.

findings.evidence: The added get_by_ids batch is followed by DocumentService.get_tenant_id(doc_id) inside the per-document loop at line 646.
findings.request: Include tenant information in the batch query or fetch it with one bulk join.
findings.reason: The document path still performs one database tenant lookup per deleted document, leaving the claimed database-I/O improvement incomplete.

findings.evidence: Document.name is globally non-unique; the new helper filters only by name, and api_app.py:636-660 derives each matched document's tenant and deletes its database, index, file linkage, and storage data without comparing ownership to the token tenant.
findings.reason: Any authenticated tenant can delete every other tenant's document sharing a requested filename.
